_comment: Expected text for the 30 frozen quads in faithful_boxes.json, transcribed by reading a contact sheet of the cropped strips. Used to score CER so accuracy changes are measured rather than eyeballed. Both models read the SAME strips, so any difference is the model's, not the crop's.

_provenance.transcribed_by: reading parity-strip contact sheets (one image, 2x zoom, index + direction label per strip)
_provenance.method: vertical strips rotated CCW to horizontal, so text reads left-to-right in the sheet
_provenance.confidence: hand-transcribed, not machine-derived. Glyphs that were ambiguous are marked with a leading '~' and are excluded from strict CER.
_provenance.caveat: Review before trusting: this is one human (AI) reading of 30 short lines. It is a better yardstick than eyeballing decoded output, but it is not a published transcript.

baseline_2026_10_02._note: Measured on this fixture with no right-margin (parity harness build_strips omits stripToTensor's PAD_MARGIN). Re-measure after touching the crop or the alphabets.
baseline_2026_10_02.conclusion: On this hand-lettered vertical-Japanese page the bundled int8 model is the more accurate of the two (CER 0.051 vs 0.174). PP-OCRv5's residual errors are real misreads - ka/kana substitutions such as 髪->髮, じゃあ->じあ - not punctuation width, which accounts for only 4 of 24. PP-OCRv5 stays optional and is NOT promoted as a default.

open_questions._note: Measured on ONE page of 30 vertical hand-lettered lines. Not grounds for a code change; each needs device confirmation.

pad_margin.finding: Adding stripToTensor's 16px white right margin appears to HURT the bundled model on this fixture: CER 0.051 (no margin) vs 0.116 (16px), monotonically worse up to 48px.
pad_margin.counter_evidence: PAD_MARGIN is a deliberate constant documented as preventing trailing-char truncation ('Saka' -> 'Sakamoto', 'neene' -> 'neenee'), presumably measured on device.
pad_margin.why_not_changed: parity build_strips does not apply the margin at all, so this compares a no-margin harness against the production path on 30 lines. The harness also differs from the app (no stripPad, no unsharp). Contradicting a device-tuned constant on one page is not evidence.
pad_margin.how_to_settle: Run the app on device with PAD_MARGIN=0 vs 16 over several chapters and compare lines read / CER.

ppocrv5_vs_bundled.finding: Bundled int8 CER 0.051 vs PP-OCRv5 0.174 on this page. PP-OCRv5 is smaller (16.6MB vs 43.6MB) but less accurate on hand-lettered text.
ppocrv5_vs_bundled.not_settled: One page, vertical text only, no horizontal, no printed-text control (no CJK font available on the host to render the same strings). PP-OCRv5 may well be better on printed or cleaner text.
ppocrv5_vs_bundled.how_to_settle: Score both on a few pages of each: hand-lettered and digitally-lettered, vertical and horizontal.

punctuation_width.finding: PP-OCRv5 emits half-width ? ! . , while the bundled model and normal Japanese use full-width. Folding half to full accounts for 4 of 24 errors (CER 0.174 -> 0.145).
punctuation_width.both_forms_present: ppocrv5_dict.txt contains BOTH '?' (id 16177) and '？' (id 16372), likewise !/！ and ./。 - so this is a model preference, not a vocabulary gap.
punctuation_width.not_changed: Folding is a display/normalisation decision affecting the translation prompt, not an OCR fix. Needs a decision on whether OCR output should be normalised or left as the model read it.
